deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the GKE Hub feature. Allowing deletion without protection could cause accidental or unauthorised removal, resulting in service disruption and loss of availability.

labels.description:
GCP labels for this Feature.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: GCP labels for this Feature This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

location.rationale: Controls where the GKE Hub feature is deployed. Restricting deployment to approved locations supports data-residency, sovereignty, and organisational compliance requirements.

name.description: The full, unique name of this Feature resource
name.rationale: The full, unique name of this Feature resource This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the owning GCP project. The correct project is specific to each team and environment; access to projects should be governed through IAM and provisioning controls rather than a generic value constraint on this resource.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Config Management spec

Set this field to MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC to enable Config Sync auto-upgrades, and set this field to MANAGEMENT_MANUAL or MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED to disable Config Sync auto-upgrades. Possible values: ["MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED", "MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC", "MANAGEMENT_MANUAL"]
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Chooses automatic or manual component management. Both modes can be operated securely, and the appropriate choice depends on the organisation's release and maintenance process rather than a universal security rule.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Version of Config Sync installed
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Selects a component or upgrade version. Secure versions change over time and depend on compatibility and support requirements, so a static generic constraint in this resource would quickly become inaccurate; version governance belongs in the release process.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: ConfigSync configuration for the cluster

Enables the installation of ConfigSync. If set to true, ConfigSync resources will be created and the other ConfigSync fields will be applied if exist. If set to false, all other ConfigSync fields will be ignored, ConfigSync resources will be deleted. If omitted, ConfigSync resources will be managed depends on the presence of the git or oci field.
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Enables an optional platform capability. Whether it is required depends on the team's architecture and operating model, and disabling it does not by itself create an insecure configuration that can be prevented by a universal policy on this resource.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The Email of the Google Cloud Service Account (GSA) used for exporting Config Sync metrics to Cloud Monitoring. The GSA should have the Monitoring Metric Writer(roles/monitoring.metricWriter) IAM role. The Kubernetes ServiceAccount 'default' in the namespace 'config-management-monitoring' should be bound to the GSA.
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Google service account used to export Config Sync metrics. Requiring an explicit approved identity reduces the risk of unintended permissions or use of an ungoverned default identity.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Set to true to enable the Config Sync admission webhook to prevent drifts. If set to 'false', disables the Config Sync admission webhook and does not prevent drifts.
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Controls Config Sync drift prevention. Enabling the webhook can strengthen enforcement, but its suitability depends on workload compatibility and the team's change-management model, so it is not a safe universal constraint for every fleet.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Specifies whether the Config Sync Repo is in hierarchical or unstructured mode
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies whether the Config Sync Repo is in hierarchical or unstructured mode This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Git repo configuration for the cluster
The Google Cloud Service Account Email used for auth when secretType is gcpServiceAccount
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Google service account used by Config Sync for Git access. Enforcing an explicit approved identity supports least privilege and prevents an unintended default identity from accessing the repository.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: URL for the HTTPS Proxy to be used when communicating with the Git repo
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies an environment-specific HTTPS proxy endpoint. A policy cannot identify one universally trusted proxy without team or network context; proxy trust and egress restrictions should be enforced by network controls.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The path within the Git repository that represents the top level of the repo to sync
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: The path within the Git repository that represents the top level of the repo to sync This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Type of secret configured for access to the Git repo
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Selects a supported repository authentication mechanism. The secure choice depends on repository type and the organisation's credential architecture, so no single value is universally appropriate; credential permissions and storage should be governed separately.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The branch of the repository to sync from. Default: master
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Selects the repository branch used by Config Sync. The trusted value is team-specific and cannot be derived generically from this resource; repository protection and deployment approval controls should establish trust.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The URL of the Git repository to use as the source of truth
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Identifies the Git repository used as the Config Sync source of truth. Restricting this to an approved repository prevents untrusted configuration from being propagated across fleet workloads.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Git revision (tag or hash) to check out. Default HEAD
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Selects the Git revision consumed by Config Sync. Requiring an approved, immutable revision reduces the risk of unreviewed or malicious configuration being deployed.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Period in seconds between consecutive syncs. Default: 15
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Sets the synchronization interval. This is primarily an operational trade-off involving rollout speed, load, and cost; there is no single interval that universally improves security for every fleet.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: OCI repo configuration for the cluster
The Google Cloud Service Account Email used for auth when secretType is gcpServiceAccount
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Google service account used to access the OCI configuration source. Requiring an explicit approved identity supports least privilege and prevents unintended repository access.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The absolute path of the directory that contains the local resources. Default: the root directory of the image
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: The absolute path of the directory that contains the local resources. Default: the root directory of the image This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Type of secret configured for access to the Git repo
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Controls the authentication mechanism used to access the OCI configuration source. Restricting it to an approved credential type helps prevent insecure or unmanaged authentication.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The OCI image repository URL for the package to sync from
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Identifies the OCI repository used as the Config Sync source of truth. Restricting it to an approved repository prevents untrusted configuration images from being deployed.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Period in seconds between consecutive syncs. Default: 15
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Sets the synchronization interval. This is primarily an operational trade-off involving rollout speed, load, and cost; there is no single interval that universally improves security for every fleet.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Version of Config Sync installed
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Selects the OCI artifact version used by Config Sync. The platform accepts supported release values, and no universally secure static version can be defined because supported versions change over time; version governance should enforce currently supported releases.

fleet_default_member_config.mesh.managem.description: Whether to automatically manage Service Mesh Possible values: ["MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED", "MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC", "MANAGEMENT_MANUAL"]
fleet_default_member_config.mesh.managem.rationale: Controls whether service-mesh components receive automatic or manual lifecycle management. Enforcing an approved mode helps ensure security patches and supported component versions are applied consistently.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Policy Controller spec
Configures the version of Policy Controller
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls the Policy Controller version deployed to the fleet. Enforcing an organisation-approved supported version reduces exposure to known vulnerabilities and unsupported components.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Configuration of Policy Controller
Interval for Policy Controller Audit scans (in seconds). When set to 0, this disables audit functionality altogether.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Sets the Policy Controller audit interval. A value of zero disables audit, but an appropriate non-zero frequency depends on fleet size, performance, and monitoring requirements, so this assessment does not prescribe a universal value constraint.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: The maximum number of audit violations to be stored in a constraint. If not set, the internal default of 20 will be used.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Limits how many audit violations are retained per constraint. The suitable value depends on fleet scale and observability capacity; it affects reporting volume rather than whether policy enforcement itself is secure.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: The set of namespaces that are excluded from Policy Controller checks. Namespaces do not need to currently exist on the cluster.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Lists namespaces exempted from policy checks. Exemptions can affect coverage, but legitimate namespaces are organisation- and workload-specific, so a generic policy cannot determine an approved list without external context.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Configures the mode of the Policy Controller installation Possible values: ["INSTALL_SPEC_UNSPECIFIED", "INSTALL_SPEC_NOT_INSTALLED", "INSTALL_SPEC_ENABLED", "INSTALL_SPEC_SUSPENDED", "INSTALL_SPEC_DETACHED"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Selects the Policy Controller installation state. Some fleets intentionally suspend, detach, or omit this component under other control models, so one installation state cannot be required securely across every team.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Logs all denies and dry run failures.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls logging of denied and dry-run policy violations. Enabling security-denial telemetry supports auditing, incident investigation, and visibility into attempted policy violations.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Enables the ability to mutate resources using Policy Controller.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls whether Policy Controller can automatically mutate admitted workloads. Because mutation changes workload configuration, it must be explicitly governed to prevent unintended or unsafe modifications.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Enables the ability to use Constraint Templates that reference to objects other than the object currently being evaluated.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Enables policies that reference other Kubernetes objects. This expands policy capability but is only needed by particular constraint templates; enabling or disabling it is not inherently secure without knowing the deployed policy set.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Map of deployment configs to deployments ("admission", "audit", "mutation").
The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Identifies the Policy Controller deployment component being configured. This is a structural selector and does not independently enable, disable, or weaken a security control.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Pod affinity configuration. Possible values: ["AFFINITY_UNSPECIFIED", "NO_AFFINITY", "ANTI_AFFINITY"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Pod affinity configuration. Possible values: ["AFFINITY_UNSPECIFIED", "NO_AFFINITY", "ANTI_AFFINITY"] This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Pod replica count.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Pod replica count This setting depends on workload or operational context, and the resource does not provide enough information to define a single organisation-independent constraint that would always improve security.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Container resource requirements.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for use by the running container.
CPU requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Configures container cpu allocation for Policy Controller. Safe sizing depends on fleet scale and workload demand, so a generic value could cause either resource pressure or unnecessary reservation rather than universally improving security.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Memory requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Configures container memory allocation for Policy Controller. Safe sizing depends on fleet scale and workload demand, so a generic value could cause either resource pressure or unnecessary reservation rather than universally improving security.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Requests describes the amount of compute resources reserved for the container by the kube-scheduler.
CPU requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Configures container cpu allocation for Policy Controller. Safe sizing depends on fleet scale and workload demand, so a generic value could cause either resource pressure or unnecessary reservation rather than universally improving security.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Memory requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Sets the memory requested by Policy Controller containers. Enforcing an approved non-zero resource request helps prevent resource starvation and supports the reliable availability of security enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Pod tolerations of node taints.
Matches a taint effect.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls which taint effects Policy Controller pods may tolerate. Restricting this value supports secure scheduling and ensures security components run only on approved node classes.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Matches a taint key (not necessarily unique).
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Identifies the node taint key tolerated by Policy Controller pods. Restricting it to an approved key prevents security components from being scheduled onto unintended nodes.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Matches a taint operator.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls how Policy Controller tolerations match node taints. Enforcing an approved operator prevents overly broad tolerations and supports workload isolation.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Matches a taint value.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Specifies the taint value tolerated by Policy Controller pods. Restricting it to an approved value supports controlled placement of security components on designated nodes.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Monitoring specifies the configuration of monitoring Policy Controller.

Specifies the list of backends Policy Controller will export to. An empty list would effectively disable metrics export. Possible values: ["MONITORING_BACKEND_UNSPECIFIED", "PROMETHEUS", "CLOUD_MONITORING"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls where Policy Controller telemetry is exported. Requiring an approved monitoring backend preserves security visibility, auditing, and detection of policy-enforcement problems.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Specifies the desired policy content on the cluster.
Configures which bundles to install and their corresponding install specs.
The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Identifies the Policy Controller bundle installed across the fleet. Restricting bundles to approved security baselines prevents unreviewed or inappropriate policy content from being enforced.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: The set of namespaces to be exempted from the bundle.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines namespaces excluded from a policy bundle. Unrestricted exemptions can create enforcement blind spots, so namespace exclusions must be explicitly approved and monitored.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Configures the installation of the Template Library.
Configures the manner in which the template library is installed on the cluster. Possible values: ["INSTALLATION_UNSPECIFIED", "NOT_INSTALLED", "ALL"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls installation of the Policy Controller template library. Enforcing the approved installation state ensures required policy-enforcement capabilities remain available.

spec.description: Optional. Hub-wide Feature configuration. If this Feature does not support any Hub-wide configuration, this field may be unused.

spec.clusterupgrade.upstream_fleets.description: Specified if other fleet should be considered as a source of upgrades. Currently, at most one upstream fleet is allowed. The fleet name should be either fleet project number or id.
spec.clusterupgrade.upstream_fleets.rationale: Identifies upstream fleets authorised to control upgrade sequencing. Restricting this trust relationship prevents an unapproved fleet from influencing cluster upgrades.

spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.description: Post conditions to override for the specified upgrade.
Amount of time to "soak" after a rollout has been finished before marking it COMPLETE. Cannot exceed 30 days.
spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.rationale: Defines the validation period after an overridden GKE upgrade. Enforcing an approved soaking period helps detect instability or security regressions before further rollout.

spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.description: Name of the upgrade, e.g., "k8s_control_plane". It should be a valid upgrade name. It must not exceet 99 characters.
spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.rationale: Identifies the upgrade targeted by an override. Restricting overrides to approved upgrade paths prevents unreviewed changes to the fleet upgrade process.

spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.description: Version of the upgrade, e.g., "1.22.1-gke.100". It should be a valid version. It must not exceet 99 characters.
spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.rationale: Specifies the version targeted by a GKE upgrade override. Enforcing supported, approved versions reduces exposure to vulnerable or untested releases.

spec.clusterupgrade.post_conditions.description: Post conditions to override for the specified upgrade.

spec.clusterupgrade.post_conditions.soak.description: Amount of time to "soak" after a rollout has been finished before marking it COMPLETE. Cannot exceed 30 days.
spec.clusterupgrade.post_conditions.soak.rationale: Defines the fleet-wide observation period after an upgrade. Requiring an approved soaking period limits rapid propagation of unstable or insecure changes across clusters.

spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.description: Specified if fleet logging feature is enabled for the entire fleet. If UNSPECIFIED, fleet logging feature is disabled for the entire fleet.

spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.d.description: Specified if applying the default routing config to logs not specified in other configs.
Specified if fleet logging feature is enabled. Possible values: ["MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "COPY", "MOVE"]
spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.d.rationale: Controls how fleet logs are routed to the fleet host project. Selecting MODE_UNSPECIFIED disables fleet logging and may reduce visibility into security events. COPY or MOVE also affects log availability in source projects, so the mode should follow the organisation's approved logging and retention requirements.

spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.f.description: Specified if applying the routing config to all logs for all fleet scopes.
Specified if fleet logging feature is enabled. Possible values: ["MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "COPY", "MOVE"]
spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.f.rationale: Controls routing of fleet-scope logs. Enforcing an approved non-disabled mode preserves central security telemetry, auditing, and incident-investigation visibility.

spec.multiclusteringress.config_membersh.description: Fully-qualified Membership name which hosts the MultiClusterIngress CRD. Example: 'projects/foo-proj/locations/global/memberships/bar'
spec.multiclusteringress.config_membersh.rationale: Identifies the fleet membership authorised to host MultiClusterIngress configuration. Restricting it to an approved membership prevents an untrusted cluster from controlling ingress exposure.

spec.rbacrolebindingactuation.allowed_cu.description: The list of allowed custom roles (ClusterRoles). If a custom role is not part of this list, it cannot be used in a fleet scope RBACRoleBinding. If a custom role in this list is in use, it cannot be removed from the list until the scope RBACRolebindings using it are deleted.
spec.rbacrolebindingactuation.allowed_cu.rationale: Defines custom roles permitted in fleet-level role bindings. Restricting this allowlist prevents overly broad or unapproved privileges from being granted across the fleet.

spec.workloadidentity.scope_tenancy_pool.description: Pool to be used for Workload Identity. This pool in trust-domain mode is used with Fleet Tenancy, so that sameness can be enforced. ex: projects/example/locations/global/workloadidentitypools/custompool
spec.workloadidentity.scope_tenancy_pool.rationale: Defines the Workload Identity tenancy trust domain. Requiring an explicit approved pool prevents workloads from trusting an unintended identity boundary.
